sentences.en: How are you in general about giving advice?
sentences.zh: 你平时给别人建议时感觉如何？
这让我感到非常不自在。

sentences.en: See, I knew this about you.
It makes me very nervous, unless I've known you a really long time, like if you're a very
sentences.zh: 这让我非常紧张，除非我认识你很久了，比如你是非常

sentences.zh: 亲密的朋友或家人，那样我才了解你，你懂吗？

sentences.en: But if I don't know you, I get nervous that I'm going to lead you astray.
sentences.zh: 但如果我不了解你，我会担心自己会把你带偏。

sentences.en: So I have some, I'm nervous-sided, I guess you could say, about today.
sentences.zh: 所以我对今天的内容感到有些紧张，我想可以这么说。

sentences.en: I don't like to give unsolicited advice.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢主动给别人建议。

有时候这只是聊天，你懂吗？

sentences.en: I'll tell someone I'm gluten-free, and they might recommend a product to me, and I like
sentences.zh: 我会告诉别人我不吃麸质，他们可能会给我推荐产品，我挺喜欢

sentences.zh: 但我得告诉你，我确实很喜欢给别人建议。

my own life and strategize and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我自己的生活，制定策略之类的。

sentences.en: So I kind of like it.
That's what I'm saying, I guess.

sentences.en: So maybe that part of me will open up in doing this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以也许做这个播客能让我那一部分性格展现出来。

sentences.en: Well, Jenna, Sam, Cassie, before we start opening up these letters from folks,
sentences.zh: 好了，珍娜、萨姆、卡西，在开始拆开大家的来信之前，

sentences.en: I thought you might be curious to know the top 10 office gripes that I found online.
sentences.zh: 我想你们可能会好奇我在网上找到的办公室十大抱怨。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll get letters about this.
sentences.zh: 也许我们会收到关于这些的来信。

sentences.en: This is like a little bit of preparation.
sentences.zh: 这算是一点小小的准备工作。

sentences.en: I'm not going to be able to help anybody with that problem.
sentences.zh: 我可帮不了任何人解决那个问题。

sentences.en: Number two, computers being slow, which wouldn't that be IT issues?
sentences.zh: 第二名，电脑运行缓慢，这难道不属于IT问题吗？
第三名，说话声音大的人。

sentences.en: I know we have some letters about that.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们有一些关于这个的来信。

sentences.en: Number four, people who have conversations right behind your desk.
sentences.zh: 第四名，在你的办公桌后面聊天的人。

sentences.en: I'm also like, wait, then you're overhearing them.
sentences.zh: 我还在想，等等，那你肯定会听到他们的谈话。

sentences.en: Number five, people who leave dirty dishes in the work sink.
sentences.zh: 第五名，在公司水槽里留下脏碗筷的人。

sentences.en: Well, I think we know how Pam feels about people not cleaning the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们都知道帕姆对那些不打扫厨房的人是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Number six, when someone calls in sick when you know they aren't sick.
sentences.zh: 第六名，明明没病却请病假的人。

sentences.en: Number seven, I didn't see this one coming.
sentences.zh: 第七名，我没料到会是这个。

sentences.en: Number eight, printers breaking down, which, again, I think could go under IT issues.
sentences.zh: 第八条，打印机坏了，我觉得这也可以归入IT问题。

sentences.en: Number nine, coming into work when you are sick.
sentences.zh: 第九条，生病时还要来上班。

sentences.en: So there's people that are like, don't fake it, but don't also bring your germs to work.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人会说，别装病，但也别把病菌带到办公室。

sentences.en: And then number 10, people who take things from your desk without asking.
sentences.zh: 第十条，不问自取拿走你桌上东西的人。

sentences.en: This happens to receptionists all the time.
sentences.zh: 前台接待员经常遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: As a person who was a real receptionist,
sentences.zh: 作为曾经真正做过前台的人，

sentences.en: people, they come by and they take your pens, they take your stapler, they take a piece of paper,
sentences.zh: 人们走过来拿走你的笔、订书机、纸张，

sentences.en: and they don't bring them back.
Well, when I was looking this up online,
Jenna, there is a lot of chatter out there about workplace etiquette.
sentences.zh: 珍娜，网上关于职场礼仪的讨论非常多。

sentences.en: Well, like I told you, Angela, we got 1,500 letters in one week.
sentences.zh: 就像我告诉你的，安吉拉，我们一周内收到了1500封信。

sentences.en: Well, then we've got a lot of work to do, Jenna.
sentences.zh: 那我们有很多工作要做，珍娜。

sentences.en: Why don't we take a break?
And when we come back, we're going to get to it.
sentences.zh: 回来之后，我们就开始处理。

sentences.en: We are back, and I'm going to share our very first letter on Dear Office Ladies.
sentences.zh: 我们回来了，我要分享《亲爱的办公室女士》的第一封来信。

sentences.en: Now, some of you have let us know to not use your full name.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们有些人告诉我们不要使用全名。

sentences.en: So this is from T in Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 所以这封信来自明尼阿波利斯的T。

sentences.en: Dear Office Ladies, I work downtown, and our company has recently moved into a new building.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的办公室女士，我在市中心工作，我们公司最近搬进了新大楼。

sentences.en: There's an extremely long hallway, maybe 150 feet, that is a buffer between the bullpen and the elevator banks.
sentences.zh: 那里有一条极长的走廊，大约150英尺，是大办公室和电梯间之间的缓冲地带。

sentences.en: I need to pause in her letter for one second.
I went on this website where you can get a visual cue for how long something is or how far or how wide, right?
sentences.zh: 我上了一个网站，可以直观地看到某样东西有多长、多远或多宽，对吧？

sentences.en: The website I went to is called measuringlee.com.
So, for you folks that need a visual cue, like I do, 150 feet is about the length of two and a half bowling alleys.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于像我一样需要直观参考的朋友们，150英尺大约是两个半保龄球道的长度。

sentences.en: This is a very long hallway.
Yes, and T has to walk down this hallway because that is where the restrooms are.
sentences.zh: 是的，T必须走过这条走廊，因为洗手间在那边。

sentences.en: T said, while using said hallway, I encounter people walking in the opposite direction, but they're so far away,
sentences.zh: T说，走这条走廊时，我会遇到迎面走来的人，但他们离得太远了，

sentences.en: I can't figure out how many strides away I should be before I acknowledge them.
sentences.zh: 我不知道在打招呼之前应该离他们多少步才合适。

sentences.en: Do I shout my greetings the second I see them?
sentences.zh: 我是一看到他们就大声问候吗？

sentences.en: It's a conundrum from yours, truly, a socially awkward person.
sentences.zh: 这是一个难题，来自一个社交尴尬的人。

sentences.en: Oh, man, did I feel this.
I feel like this happens to me sometimes at drop-off and pick-up at school.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我在学校接送孩子时有时也会遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: You see people from so far away.
sentences.zh: 你会看到远处走来的人。

sentences.en: And when do you do the nod and the wave?
sentences.zh: 那你什么时候点头示意或挥手打招呼呢？
你什么时候做这个动作？

sentences.en: I have a trick for this.
I call it the hangnail trick.
You can also use your phone, but if you don't have your phone.
sentences.zh: 你也可以用手机，但如果你没带手机的话。

sentences.en: Do you fidget and look at your fingers?
sentences.zh: 你会局促不安地盯着自己的手指看吗？

sentences.en: I pretend like I have a hangnail I'm investigating so I can look down at my hands until I can feel that I'm closer.
sentences.zh: 我会假装在研究手指上的倒刺，这样就能低头看手，直到感觉距离差不多了。

sentences.en: And then you look up and then you acknowledge.
sentences.zh: 然后你再抬头，打个招呼。

sentences.en: So that way you don't get like the awkward eye contact from too far away.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不会在距离太远时，陷入那种尴尬的对视中。

sentences.en: And then you have to like continue the eye contact all the way down the bowling alley.
sentences.zh: 不然你就得像在保龄球馆一样，一路保持着眼神交流。

sentences.en: How long do I keep eye contact?
sentences.zh: 我该保持多久的眼神交流呢？

sentences.en: So one, I would say carry your phone with you because then you can be absorbed in something.
sentences.zh: 所以第一，我会建议你随身带手机，这样你就可以假装沉浸在某件事里。

sentences.en: If you don't have your phone, check your hangnail.
sentences.zh: 如果你没带手机，就检查一下你的倒刺。

sentences.en: Basically have an item of business.
That gets you down the hallway to avoid this conundrum.
sentences.zh: 这样你走过走廊时就能避免这种困境。

sentences.en: So then when you pass someone, you just pass them right at the moment and just say, hi.
sentences.zh: 所以当你经过某人时，就在擦肩而过的那一刻说声“嗨”。
我真的很喜欢这个方法。

sentences.en: I think I am so bad at this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我在这方面太差劲了。

sentences.en: I often wave the minute I see someone.
sentences.zh: 我经常一看到人就挥手。

sentences.en: So I would wave way at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以我会在刚看到的时候就挥手。

sentences.en: And then I feel no pressure.
And then when I get right near you, I'd be like, hey.
sentences.zh: 然后等我走到你跟前时，我会说，嘿。

sentences.en: So this wouldn't cause you anxiety, this long hallway.
sentences.zh: 所以这种长走廊不会让你感到焦虑吗？

sentences.en: Not if I get my wave in at the top.
sentences.zh: 除非我在顶端就先挥手。

sentences.en: Now I can just be in my own skin.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以自在地做我自己了。

sentences.en: Sometimes I've done that and the person has not waved back from afar.
sentences.zh: 有时候我这样做，但对方在远处并没有挥手回应。

sentences.en: Oh, then I do get in my head.
sentences.zh: 哦，那我就开始胡思乱想了。

sentences.en: This is when you get your hangnail.
sentences.zh: 这时候你就会长倒刺了。

sentences.en: This is when I'm going to look at my fingers.
sentences.zh: 这时候我就会盯着自己的手指看。

sentences.en: T, thank you for writing us.
Item of business are just wave right at the top.
sentences.zh: 要点就是要在刚见面时就挥手。

sentences.en: Our next question is from JC in Indiana.
sentences.zh: 下一个问题来自印第安纳州的JC。

sentences.en: Here's what JC had to say.
My office bathroom is small, but it has a small couch in it.
sentences.zh: 我的办公室洗手间很小，但里面有个小沙发。

sentences.en: Lately, when I've wanted to use the restroom, our office receptionist is on the couch,
sentences.zh: 最近，每当我想用洗手间时，我们的前台接待员都在沙发上，

sentences.en: on the phone, texting, or otherwise relaxing.
sentences.zh: 要么在打电话，要么在发短信，或者在休息。

sentences.en: My question is, who wants to relax in an office bathroom?
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，谁会想在办公室洗手间里休息啊？
还有人遇到过这种情况吗？

sentences.en: I find the interaction awkward at best, given I am not there to relax on the couch.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这种互动简直尴尬透了，毕竟我不是去那里躺在沙发上休息的。

sentences.en: Well, JC, you might remember that a certain someone at Dunder Mifflin spent some time on
sentences.zh: 嗯，JC，你可能记得《办公室风云》里的某个人曾在

sentences.en: a couch in the woman's restroom.
sentences.zh: 女洗手间的沙发上待过。

sentences.en: It was so, even though we were just like pretending, it was still so awkward.
sentences.zh: 那真是，即使我们只是在演戏，依然觉得非常尴尬。

sentences.en: Just the idea of having someone lounge in the restroom.
sentences.zh: 光是想到有人在洗手间里闲逛就受不了。

sentences.en: Because when you got to go, you need no one out there, you know?
sentences.zh: 因为当你需要上厕所时，你不想外面有任何人，你懂吗？

sentences.en: I would have a very hard time tinkling.
I mean, I get, what do you call it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我有那个，怎么说来着？

sentences.en: But so, you know, sometimes what I do is I do the flush and go.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，有时候我会采取冲水的同时进行。

sentences.en: You flush and pee at the same time?

sentences.zh: 那样不会溅到屁股上吗？

sentences.en: No, I'll tell you something I don't do.
sentences.zh: 不，我告诉你一件我不会做的事。

sentences.en: I do not hover or squat over a toilet seat.
sentences.zh: 我上厕所时从不悬空或蹲在马桶圈上。

sentences.en: And I find the whole practice very annoying.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这种做法非常烦人。

sentences.en: Because the people who do spray the seat, and most of the time they don't clean it up.
sentences.zh: 因为那些会溅到马桶圈上的人，大多数时候根本不清理。

sentences.en: And I really got upset about this when I was pregnant.
sentences.zh: 我怀孕的时候对此真的感到很抓狂。

sentences.en: Because, you know, when you definitely can't hover, when you've got a giant pregger's belly.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，挺着个大肚子的时候，你根本没法悬空。

sentences.en: I got to sit down and go.
But first, I'm cleaning up someone else's spray.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我得先清理别人溅上去的尿渍。

sentences.en: You know the little liner things that you can put?
sentences.zh: 你知道那种可以铺在马桶上的垫纸吗？

sentences.en: My stream isn't strong enough to get the flap out of the way.
sentences.zh: 我的尿流不够强，冲不开中间那块垂下来的纸片。

sentences.en: So then the flap of the liner can come back.
sentences.zh: 所以那块纸片就会反弹回来。

sentences.en: So I do two little strips of toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 所以我通常会撕两小条卫生纸。

sentences.en: And I make my own little seat.
JC, I don't know why the receptionist is in there texting and on the phone and all that.
sentences.zh: JC，我不知道为什么前台接待员会在那儿发短信、打电话之类的。

sentences.en: My guess is maybe there's no break room, nowhere for her to go, to just be off the clock, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 我猜可能是因为没有休息室，她没地方去，没法真正地“下班”休息。
这是我第一个想到的问题。

sentences.en: If that's not true, JC, if there is a break room, this is what I think you should do.
sentences.zh: 如果不是这样，JC，如果确实有休息室，我觉得你应该这么做。

sentences.en: I think maybe you get the keys to the office on a Saturday morning.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你可以找个周六早上拿到办公室钥匙。

sentences.en: Whenever someone's not there, hear me out.
sentences.zh: 趁没人的时候，听我说完。

sentences.en: Jenna's giving me such a look.
sentences.zh: 珍娜正用那种眼神看着我。

sentences.en: You get rid of the sofa.
Well, then there's nowhere to sit and hang out.
sentences.zh: 那这样就没地方坐着闲聊了。
那里就会变成一个非休闲区。

sentences.en: So your solution is get rid of the couch.
sentences.zh: 所以你的解决方案就是把沙发扔了？

sentences.en: Or you could, you know, be an adult and just talk to the receptionist and say, hey, when you're in here, I can't go-go because you're in here and it's awkward.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以，你知道的，成熟一点，直接跟前台说：嘿，你在里面的时候，我没法上厕所，因为你在里面会很尴尬。

sentences.en: I mean, JC, you're probably not the only person that is having this problem.
sentences.zh: 我是说，JC，你可能不是唯一遇到这个问题的人。

sentences.en: You would be the hero of the office.
sentences.zh: 你会成为办公室的英雄。

sentences.en: You could just confront it head on.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接正面解决它。

sentences.en: Or, I suppose, break into the office after hours and remove the couch.
sentences.zh: 或者，我想，在下班后潜入办公室把沙发搬走。

sentences.en: Who wants to be in there?
Everyone stop hanging out in your bathrooMs.
sentences.zh: 大家都别在洗手间里闲逛了。

sentences.en: I mean, listen, sometimes you do go to the bathroom and get chatty.
sentences.zh: 我是说，听着，有时候你确实会去洗手间然后聊起天来。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like if you and I were, like, we went to a ladies' room, we might have a combo where we're washing our hands.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得如果我们俩，比如我们去了女洗手间，我们在洗手时可能会聊上几句。

sentences.en: That is not what we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我们现在讨论的不是这个。

sentences.en: Don't hang out on a sofa in a bathroom.
sentences.zh: 别在洗手间的沙发上闲逛。
这是一个禁止沙发闲聊区。

sentences.en: If you put a sofa in there, someone's going to sit on it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在那儿放张沙发，肯定会有人去坐。

sentences.en: Our next letter is from AR in Syracuse.
AR says, how do I tell a coworker to take private calls not on speakerphone?
sentences.zh: AR问，我该怎么告诉同事不要开免提接听私人电话？

sentences.en: This person frequently is talking to banks, doctors, their mom about very specific personal matters while I'm trying to work, and it makes it difficult to focus.
sentences.zh: 这人经常在我要工作的时候，用免提跟银行、医生或她妈妈谈论非常具体的私事，这让我很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: I know way too much about their personal life because they're always on speakerphone.
sentences.zh: 因为她总是开着免提，我对她的私生活了解得太多了。

sentences.en: Also, this person happens to be my supervisor.
sentences.zh: 而且，这人还是我的上司。

sentences.en: This is a little bit of a pet peeve of mine.

sentences.zh: 我什么都不会蘸牧场沙拉酱吃。

sentences.en: I do enjoy mixing mayo and ketchup.
sentences.zh: 我确实喜欢把蛋黄酱和番茄酱混在一起。

sentences.en: And like throwing that maybe on a burger.
sentences.zh: 然后把它涂在汉堡上之类的。

sentences.en: I also like whatever that thing is, that like Thousand Island dressing with relish in it
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢那种东西，就是那种加了调味酱的千岛酱，

sentences.en: that we're throwing on the Big Mac.
sentences.zh: 就是我们涂在巨无霸上的那种。

sentences.en: That's similar to your mayo ketchup mix.
sentences.zh: 那和你调的蛋黄酱番茄酱混合酱差不多。
所以我挺喜欢那些东西的。

sentences.en: But if sauces disappeared, if all the sauces you just listed disappeared, it would be barely
sentences.zh: 但如果酱料消失了，如果你刚才列举的所有酱料都消失了，对我来说几乎

sentences.en: Oh, it'd be a sad day for me.
sentences.zh: 噢，那对我来说可真是悲伤的一天。

sentences.en: I love the different tastes in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢嘴里有各种不同的味道。

sentences.en: I think that is a great way to complete that question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得用这句话来结束那个问题真是太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm going to get you a shirt that says Sauce Lady on the front.
sentences.zh: 我要给你买件T恤，前面印上“酱料女士”。

sentences.en: And on the back, it's going to say, I love all the flavors in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 背面印上“我喜欢嘴里有各种味道”。

sentences.en: I love all the flavors in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢嘴里有各种味道。

sentences.en: You best be making me that shirt.
sentences.zh: 你最好真的给我做那件T恤。

sentences.en: This next question is coming from A in Sacramento, California.
sentences.zh: 下一个问题来自加州萨克拉门托的A。

sentences.en: I am a college senior and will be starting my job hunt soon.
sentences.zh: 我是一名大四学生，很快就要开始找工作了。

sentences.en: I have started the job search, which is both exciting and terrifying at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我已经开始找工作了，这既让人兴奋又让人害怕。

sentences.en: I would love any advice when it comes to interviewing for a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 关于全职工作的面试，我很希望能得到一些建议。

sentences.en: Well, A, I love this question.
Because I actually wrote a whole chapter about interviewing in my book, The Actor's Life.
sentences.zh: 因为我在我的书《演员的生活》里专门写了一章关于面试的内容。

sentences.en: Because when I first came out to Los Angeles, I would go on a lot of general meetings, which are like interviews.
sentences.zh: 因为我刚到洛杉矶时，经常参加各种常规会议，那就像面试一样。

sentences.en: They're just sit down and talk to this producer or director or executive.
sentences.zh: 就是坐下来和制片人、导演或高管谈话。

sentences.en: I was very, very bad at them.
sentences.zh: 我当时表现得非常非常差。

sentences.en: I would think you'd be good at them.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你会很擅长呢。

sentences.en: I had to really learn how to be good in interviews.
sentences.zh: 我真的得去学学怎么在面试中表现好。

sentences.en: You know, it is a whole skill.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这完全是一项技能。

sentences.en: You can be very good at the job, but very bad at explaining that you're good at the job.
sentences.zh: 你可能非常胜任这份工作，但却很不擅长表达自己胜任这份工作。

sentences.en: So this is something that I think you have to take time and preparation with.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是你需要花时间和精力去准备的事情。

sentences.en: So I had an agent at the time, and despite my terrible interview, he decided to represent me, and then he gave me some coaching.
sentences.zh: 当时我有个经纪人，尽管我面试表现很差，他还是决定代理我，然后给了我一些指导。

sentences.en: He had some rules about how to give good interviews, good general meetings, and they're great.
sentences.zh: 他对于如何进行高质量的面试和全体会议有一些准则，而且这些准则非常棒。

sentences.en: I passed along a lot of his advice in my book, and here it is.
sentences.zh: 我在书中分享了他许多建议，现在就列在这里。

sentences.en: Rule number one, show up on time.
And by the way, on time means 10 minutes early.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，准时意味着提前10分钟到。

sentences.en: Because you have to remember you're going to need to find time to park.
sentences.zh: 因为你得记住，你还需要时间找停车位。

sentences.en: You're going to have to find the office.
You might have to go pee.
sentences.zh: 你可能还得去上个厕所。

sentences.en: Well, we would definitely need to go pee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实得去上个厕所。

sentences.en: You want to account for any unforeseen probleMs.
sentences.zh: 你要考虑到任何不可预见的问题。

sentences.en: He also said, do not bring a beverage into your interview and turn off your phone.
sentences.zh: 他还说，面试时不要带饮料，并且要关掉手机。

sentences.en: He said you would not believe how many people come in carrying a Starbucks and their phone dinging.
sentences.zh: 他说你绝对想不到有多少人带着星巴克进来，手机还叮叮响个不停。

sentences.en: He said you think you shouldn't have to give this advice, but you do.
sentences.zh: 他说你以为这种建议根本不需要给，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I think you do because my phone wouldn't ding, but I almost always show up with the iced tea.
sentences.zh: 我觉得确实需要，因为我的手机虽然不会响，但我几乎总是带着冰茶去面试。

sentences.en: He says leave your beverage in your car.
You know, this is a stranger.
sentences.zh: 要知道，对方是个陌生人。

sentences.en: You don't drink your beverage in an interview.
sentences.zh: 面试的时候不能喝饮料。

sentences.en: Second, remember, you are interviewing them too.
sentences.zh: 第二，记住，你也在面试他们。

sentences.en: An interview is like a first date.
You're there to discern whether or not this is a match.
sentences.zh: 你是去判断双方是否合适。

sentences.en: And it has to be a match for both people.
sentences.zh: 而且这对双方来说都必须是合适的。

sentences.en: It has to go both ways.
And that always brought me some comfort because it made me kind of like less needy because
sentences.zh: 这总能给我带来一些安慰，因为它让我没那么卑微，因为

sentences.en: I was remembering like, hey, I'm here to discern if I like this place too.
sentences.zh: 我记得，嘿，我也是来判断自己是否喜欢这个地方的。

sentences.en: I have a say in this.
sentences.zh: 在这件事上我有发言权。

sentences.en: And I'm going to take agency for myself.
Third, I think it's always good to be ready with some sort of icebreaker to get some banter going.
sentences.zh: 第三，我觉得准备一些破冰话题来开启闲聊总是好的。

sentences.en: You don't want to launch into your skills right away.
sentences.zh: 你不想一上来就直接推销自己的技能。

sentences.en: So what is something that could spark a connection?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么话题能引发共鸣呢？

sentences.en: Sometimes I would go in the rooms and I would kind of look around and kind of clock things.
sentences.zh: 有时我走进房间，会环顾四周，留意一些东西。

sentences.en: Like, oh, where do these people, do they have a vacation photo up?
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，这些人，他们有没有挂度假照片？

sentences.en: One time I walked in and this woman had this beautiful blue ring on.
sentences.zh: 有一次我走进去，看到一位女士戴着一枚漂亮的蓝色戒指。

sentences.en: And I said, oh, my goodness, I love your ring.
sentences.zh: 我说，天哪，我太喜欢你的戒指了。

sentences.en: And she said, oh, it's an aquamarine.
And I said, I'm a March baby.
sentences.zh: 我说，我也是三月出生的。

sentences.en: And then we had a little bonding moment about both being Pisces.
sentences.zh: 然后我们因为都是双鱼座，产生了一点共鸣。

sentences.en: I think these little things are very helpful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些小细节非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Because remember, businesses are interested in your skills and your abilities.
sentences.zh: 因为你要记住，企业不仅看重你的技能和能力。

sentences.en: But they are also going to have to, like, be around you on a personal level.
sentences.zh: 他们还得在个人层面上和你相处。
这种融洽的关系很有帮助。

sentences.en: You know, Greg Daniels once told me that people want to work with people that they think they can spend a 12-hour day with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，格雷格·丹尼尔斯曾告诉我，人们想和那些他们觉得能一起共事12小时的人一起工作。

sentences.en: And I've always thought about that.
sentences.zh: 我一直把这句话记在心里。

sentences.en: That was a little bit of, I guess, interview advice I took to heart.
sentences.zh: 我想，这算是我铭记在心的一条面试建议。

sentences.en: And then my mom said when I would go in for a big meeting, a big interview, she would say, you just go in there and you be politely bored.
sentences.zh: 我妈曾说，每当我参加重要会议或面试时，她都会告诉我，你就进去，表现得礼貌而淡定。

sentences.en: Like, they need to get you interested.
sentences.zh: 意思是，他们得想办法让你感兴趣。

sentences.en: You're not there to get them interested.
sentences.zh: 你不是去求着让他们对你感兴趣的。

sentences.en: Oh, that's another way to go, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 噢，这又是另一种思路，不是吗？

sentences.en: But you can still have an icebreaker.
sentences.zh: 但你依然可以准备一个破冰话题。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's that thing that you said where you're taking assessment of them as well.
sentences.zh: 不过，就像你说的，这也是一个你同时在评估对方的过程。

sentences.en: My next bit of advice is you know that you're going to have to talk about why you're a good fit for the job.
sentences.zh: 我的下一条建议是，你要知道你肯定会被问到为什么你适合这份工作。

sentences.en: Of all the things they might ask you, we know this is happening.
sentences.zh: 在他们可能问的所有问题中，我们确定这题必考。

sentences.en: Have a self-pitch about yourself that you can say in three sentences.
sentences.zh: 准备一段三句话以内的自我推销词。

sentences.en: Be sure that it's specific to the job description, to the company, that it's not just general.
sentences.zh: 确保内容针对职位描述和公司情况，不要泛泛而谈。

sentences.en: And finally, especially if you're interviewing for the first time or if you haven't interviewed in a while, practice with someone before you go.
sentences.zh: 最后，特别是如果你是第一次面试，或者很久没面试了，去之前一定要找人练习一下。

sentences.en: I had been going on some general meetings and nothing was happening.
sentences.zh: 当时我参加了一些常规会议，但都没什么下文。

sentences.en: And my manager said, maybe we should practice the meetings.
sentences.zh: 我的经纪人说，也许我们该演练一下这些会议。

sentences.en: So we did a practice session.
sentences.zh: 于是我们进行了一次模拟练习。

sentences.en: And in our practice session, she asked me, what kind of acting are you interested in doing, Jenna?
sentences.zh: 在练习中，她问我：珍娜，你对哪种类型的表演感兴趣？

sentences.en: And I gave the answer that I always gave.
sentences.zh: 我给出了我一贯的回答。

sentences.en: I would say, well, you know, I love comedy.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，你知道的，我喜欢喜剧。

sentences.en: I would be interested in film, television, independent film.
sentences.zh: 我对电影、电视剧、独立电影都感兴趣。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say no to a soap opera.
And she was like, let me stop you right there.
This is not the right answer.
I don't know who you are.
She said, here's your new answer.
Your answer is, I would love to be cast on an ensemble comedy television series.
sentences.zh: 你的回答是：我非常希望能出演一部群像喜剧电视剧。

sentences.en: Because obviously, you can do all these things, but you need to give people a vision of you specifically and what is your main skill.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，你可以做所有这些事情，但你需要给人们一个关于你个人的愿景，以及你最擅长的技能是什么。

sentences.en: And after I did that, my meetings really started to pay off.
sentences.zh: 在我这样做之后，我的面试真的开始有成效了。

sentences.en: I love getting specific with things.
I mean, whether it's a prayer, a meditation, a goal, get specific.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无论是祈祷、冥想还是目标，都要具体。

sentences.en: My mom always says get specific with the Lord, you know?
sentences.zh: 我妈妈总是说要向上帝具体地祈求，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I write out a goal or something I want to pray about.
sentences.zh: 我会写下一个目标或者我想祈祷的事情。

sentences.en: I write it on a Post-it note.
I put it on my bathroom mirror.

sentences.zh: 关于你这一点我很了解。

sentences.en: And I can say in my experience personally, the more specific I am, the better results I get.
sentences.zh: 我可以根据我个人的经验说，我越具体，得到的结果就越好。

sentences.en: So when you're putting it out there, folks, get specific.
sentences.zh: 所以各位，当你们在表达诉求时，要具体。

sentences.en: I would like to add one thing that I did have a job once where I hired people and I also had to fire people.
sentences.zh: 我想补充一点，我曾经有一份工作，既要负责招聘，也要负责解雇员工。

sentences.en: Oh, so you've been on the other side of this.
sentences.zh: 噢，所以你曾经站在过另一边。

sentences.en: What advice would you give someone from that position?
sentences.zh: 从那个角度来看，你会给别人什么建议？

sentences.en: I would say the minute you arrive, be polite to everyone because you don't know from the person that held the door open for you to maybe someone who helped direct where you parked.
sentences.zh: 我会说，你一到那里，就要对每个人都礼貌，因为你不知道为你开门的人，或者帮你指引停车位的人是谁。

sentences.en: All of those people that are there matter to who you're interviewing with.
sentences.zh: 所有在场的人对于你要面试的对象来说都很重要。

sentences.en: So be respectful to everyone you encounter, no matter what their position you might think, because even though their position might not dictate whether or not you get the job,
sentences.zh: 所以要尊重你遇到的每一个人，无论你认为他们的职位如何，因为即使他们的职位可能决定不了你是否能得到这份工作，
但他们对这家公司很重要。

sentences.en: And then the other thing I would say is just think about how you smell.
sentences.zh: 另外我还要说的一点是，注意一下你的气味。

sentences.en: When you go to interview with someone, you're usually in a smaller office.
sentences.zh: 当你去面试时，通常是在一个小办公室里。

sentences.en: And your smell will come in with you.
sentences.zh: 你的气味会随你一起进入房间。

sentences.en: It'll be the unique thing that walks in the room with you that sets you apart.
sentences.zh: 那将是随你进入房间的独特之处，让你与众不同。

sentences.en: Try not to overdo it with the cologne or the perfume.
sentences.zh: 尽量不要喷太浓的古龙水或香水。

sentences.en: Not saying this is going to rule you out, but there will be a thought that goes through someone's mind.
sentences.zh: 我不是说这会让你被淘汰，但别人心里难免会犯嘀咕。

sentences.en: It's kind of like, oh, my gosh, am I going to have to sit downwind of this person?
sentences.zh: 就像是，天哪，我以后是不是得坐在离这人下风口的地方？

sentences.en: Am I going to have to sit with Drakkar all the time?
sentences.zh: 我以后是不是得一直跟“德拉卡”古龙水味儿坐在一起？
整天都要闻着德拉卡味儿。

sentences.en: If your smell precedes you, think about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你的气味比你先到，那你就得考虑一下了。
萨克拉门托的A，祝你好运。

sentences.en: Our final question of the day comes from M in Oregon.
sentences.zh: 今天最后一个问题来自俄勒冈州的M。

sentences.en: M, I really feel like Angela Martin would have strong opinions about this one.
sentences.zh: M，我真的觉得安吉拉·马丁会对这个问题有强烈的看法。

sentences.en: And also, M, you are talking to three cat ladies.
sentences.zh: 而且，M，你现在是在跟三位爱猫女士对话。

sentences.en: I'm going to want you to weigh in on this, too.
sentences.zh: 我也想让你对此发表一下看法。

sentences.en: M says, I was flabbergasted when a coworker recently asked me to check up on his cats while he was away for three weeks.
sentences.zh: M说，最近有个同事让我帮他照看三周的猫，我当时惊呆了。

sentences.en: I have coworkers with whom I have friendships, and this wouldn't be a problem with them.
sentences.zh: 我有关系好的同事，如果是他们，这根本不是问题。

sentences.en: But this male colleague and I have never done much more than a casual chit-chat.
sentences.zh: 但这位男同事和我平时除了闲聊几句，基本没交集。

sentences.en: We've never seen each other outside of work and have never even had lunch together, other than a few team lunches paid for by our boss.
sentences.zh: 我们从没在工作之外见过面，除了老板请客的几次团队午餐，我们甚至没单独吃过饭。

sentences.en: It also wouldn't have been a problem if we were neighbors.
sentences.zh: 如果我们是邻居，这也不会是个问题。

sentences.en: I would totally swing by for a cat visit, even if I didn't know a neighbor very well.
sentences.zh: 哪怕邻居不太熟，我也完全愿意顺路去喂喂猫。

sentences.en: But he lives 25 minutes away from my house.
sentences.zh: 但他住的地方离我家有25分钟车程。

sentences.en: This seems like a bold ask to me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这要求提得太冒昧了。

sentences.en: I would never ask a casual work acquaintance such a favor.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会向一个普通的职场熟人提这种请求。

sentences.en: I told him that I thought it would make better sense for him to ask someone who lived a bit closer to him.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，我觉得他找个住得近点的人会更合适。

sentences.en: It was such a strange request that I can't let go of it, and my husband is tired of me talking about it.
sentences.zh: 这个请求太奇怪了，我一直耿耿于怀，我丈夫都听烦了。

sentences.en: I mean, we know what happened to Angela's cat when she asked Dwight to watch it once.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们都知道安吉拉让德怀特帮忙看猫时发生了什么。

sentences.en: I think it's a big ask for someone you don't know that well and who lives far away from you.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于一个不熟且住得远的人来说，这确实是个过分的要求。

sentences.en: Well, I would start by saying I think you handled it well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先我想说，我觉得你处理得很好。

sentences.en: I think Em's big question is how do I let this go?
sentences.zh: 我觉得M最纠结的是该怎么放下这件事？

sentences.en: I thought maybe this person just doesn't have anyone to ask.
sentences.zh: 我想也许是因为这个人没别人可以拜托了。

sentences.en: Maybe they don't have a lot of friends.
Maybe this person views you as one of the nicest people in the office.
sentences.zh: 也许这个人把你视为办公室里最友善的人之一。

sentences.en: I'm not saying this means that you have to do it.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说你非得答应不可。

sentences.en: You do not have to do it.

sentences.zh: 这确实是个不小的请求。

sentences.en: But in terms of just letting it go, maybe there's a way to frame it where you say, oh,
sentences.zh: 但如果只是想放下这件事，或许你可以换个说法，比如，噢，

sentences.en: maybe this person just doesn't have anyone else.
sentences.zh: 也许这个人真的没别人可以找了。

sentences.en: Well, Jenna, you went very zen on that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，Jenna，你这番话真是太佛系了。

sentences.en: And you really are taking the moral compass high ground here.
sentences.zh: 你确实站在了道德的制高点上。

sentences.en: And I think you have a good point.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得你说得很有道理。

sentences.en: But yeah, I would say I'm sorry I can't and never say why you can't.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我会说抱歉我帮不上忙，而且永远不要解释原因。

sentences.en: I think sometimes we feel like we have to come up with an excuse of like why you can't
sentences.zh: 我觉得有时候我们总觉得必须找个借口来解释为什么不能

sentences.en: But then, yeah, if you want to go above and beyond, maybe you can recommend like a cat
sentences.zh: 但如果你想做得更周到些，或许可以推荐一个猫咪

sentences.en: service or if you happen to know someone close by or just kind of, yeah, if you feel like
sentences.zh: 看护服务，或者如果你刚好认识附近的人，或者，如果你觉得

sentences.en: they're lonely, you can kind of like brainstorm with them like, oh, maybe there's a neighbor
